findings.summary: Ridgeline-FT achieves higher pass@1 than Plainweave-FT on Quillbench, with a statistically significant mean paired difference of 2.26 percentage points (95% CI [1.26, 3.26], Holm-adjusted p = 0.0022).
findings.scope: Quillbench (420 Python problems, greedy decoding), pass@1, 8 paired seeds
findings.caveats: Significance is adjusted for two pre-specified endpoints; result is specific to this dataset and base model.

findings.summary: Ridgeline-FT also shows a statistically significant higher compile rate than Plainweave-FT, with a mean paired difference of 2.7 percentage points (95% CI [1.19, 4.35], Holm-adjusted p = 0.0043).
findings.scope: Quillbench (420 Python problems, greedy decoding), compile rate, 8 paired seeds
findings.caveats: Secondary endpoint; significance is adjusted for two pre-specified endpoints.

findings.summary: Both fine-tuned recipes outperform the base model Fernleaf-1.3B on pass@1 (Ridgeline-FT: 47.9% vs 31.4%; Plainweave-FT: 45.6% vs 31.4%) and compile rate (93.1% and 90.4% vs 84.0%), but no statistical tests are reported for these comparisons.
findings.scope: Quillbench, pass@1 and compile rate, single deterministic base run vs 8-seed fine-tuned means
findings.caveats: Base model is a single run; differences are descriptive only, no significance tests provided.

sentences.text: On Quillbench, Ridgeline-FT achieved a significantly higher pass@1 than Plainweave-FT, with a mean paired difference of 2.26 percentage points (95% CI [1.26, 3.26], Holm-adjusted p = 0.0022).
Ridgeline-FT also showed a significantly higher compile rate than Plainweave-FT, with a mean paired difference of 2.7 percentage points (95% CI [1.19, 4.35], Holm-adjusted p = 0.0043).

Both fine-tuned recipes outperformed the base model Fernleaf-1.3B on pass@1 (Ridgeline-FT: 47.9% vs 31.4%; Plainweave-FT: 45.6% vs 31.4%) and compile rate (93.1% and 90.4% vs 84.0%), though these comparisons were descriptive only, as no statistical tests were reported.
